output.brief: FCR fell because of the 14 April Finance change, not mainly the new starters. It cut the credit an agent can apply on a call from £100 to £25 and automatically sends bigger cases to the Billing Resolution team. Billing calls referred rose from 7% to 54% that week. Referred calls resolve first time only about 33% of the time, against 82% for the rest, and that unchanged gap explains the site drop. The April intake refers at about the same rate as veterans (56% against 53–54%). Veterans' FCR fell from 75% to 67%, the same as everyone else. The new starters are not the cause. Tariff-enquiry volume doubled but those calls resolve well (85%). IVR timing doesn't match the drop. Performance plans would punish the wrong group and are harmful. Next: agree a revised in-call credit limit with Finance, with post-call sampling of credits. Trial it on two teams for six weeks, tracking FCR and the unsupported-credit rate, as the Finance controller said she would accept. The limit is a setting that takes one day to change. Do not extend nesting or pause the IVR work on this evidence. Confidence is fairly high. The main gap is that no trial has yet shown that raising the limit restores FCR.
